A zoomable reference map

Native languages
of North America

Explore Ives Goddard’s map of Native languages and language families across much of North America, focused mainly north of Mexico. The revised and enlarged edition dates to 1999. Open the full-page PDF in your browser to zoom and pan across its labels and index.

Open the zoomable Smithsonian PDF ↗Visit the historical map room ↗
Read the map’s time period carefully. This is a language-family map, not a map of every nation or a record of fixed political borders. Its published description places language areas at earliest European contact, which happened at different times in different regions. The areas are approximate, fuzzy, and may be uncertain. Its focus is north of Mexico; it does not provide full coverage of Indigenous peoples in Mexico, Central America, or the Caribbean. It should not be read as a single snapshot of North America in 1500 or as evidence that a people was absent where no label appears.

View the full map

The PDF is hosted by the Smithsonian’s National Museum of the American Indian, Native Knowledge 360°. Use your browser’s PDF controls to zoom, pan, search text where supported, or download the file from the viewer.

Map credit and scope

Native Languages and Language Families of North America, compiled by Ives Goddard; revised and enlarged edition with additions and corrections, 1999. The PDF identifies language families and linguistic units. It does not map individual nations’ territories.

The Atlas links to the Smithsonian-hosted PDF rather than copying the file. The map is a scholarly orientation reference; consult the cited sources and community accounts on individual profile pages for nation-specific histories.
